cases.trigger: An ordinary Qwen3-Omni turn deployment exposes three structured stage configs (thinker, talker, code2wav; Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration) and receives /v1/realtime without a proprietary duplex handler or explicit duplex=1 request.
cases.independent_reasoning: BaseVllmOmniStageConfig stores architecture on model_config.model_arch and role on model_stage. The base helper gets stage.engine_args with a None default; that field is absent on this typed object. Its model_arch read consequently returns None, so all(...) is false even when the live topology is eligible. dispatch_realtime_websocket necessarily invokes the generic fallback and returns before constructing the intended full-duplex connection.
cases.consequence: Every otherwise matching typed-config Qwen3 turn session follows the wrong realtime implementation. The intended conformant connection and its session/conversation/structured-error contract are bypassed. This is a deterministic compatibility failure of this supported route, not a hypothetical future field mismatch. The exact client traceback reported by the PR is not independently asserted here.
cases.severity_reason: P1 is limited to the supported Qwen3 realtime route: it is systematically disabled by the predicate under the normal producer representation. No P0, broad-project failure or data-loss claim; HTTP chat and proprietary duplex paths are outside this finding.
cases.test_reasoning: The new positive typed-topology assertion would be false on base. The full HTTP/WebSocket routing fixture also reaches the rejected branch on base. Three negative topology variants should remain false. These are source-derived expectations, not locally executed results.

cases.trigger: DiffusionWorker.shutdown is called while a rank-local LayerWiseOffloadBackend is enabled and has offloaded DiT/encoder blocks; original tensor devices are accelerators. Shutdown is disposing the model, not temporarily disabling offload for later inference.
cases.independent_reasoning: The complete base LayerWiseOffloadBackend class has no shutdown override. Virtual dispatch uses OffloadBackend.shutdown, which calls self.disable(); LayerWiseOffloadBackend.disable invokes _disable(restore_weights=True). That queues restore_next_block for every DiT hook and propagates restore_weights to encoder cleanup. Each restore allocates fresh tensor storage on the recorded original device and copies the CPU backing there. Restored tensors remain owned by the model until the worker drops model_runner after the backend call, so the whole restored model can accumulate on the accelerator during teardown.
cases.consequence: Shutdown performs a needless full model transfer and can demand the accelerator capacity that layerwise offload was selected to avoid. The concrete conditional failure is allocation failure when restoration exceeds free device memory, or bounded-shutdown overrun when the copies take too long. Worker catches backend exceptions but still incurs the transfer/allocation failure and logs it. PR-reported SIGABRT/timing measurements were not independently reproduced and are not the proof.
cases.severity_reason: P2: real lifecycle/resource bug on an opt-in path, with OOM/timeout consequences dependent on model size, free memory and timing. The source proves the unnecessary restore and concrete failure mechanism; it does not establish universal startup/inference failure, a universal 30-second overrun or P1 urgency for all deployments. It is more than P3 polish because the extra allocations can fail at process exit.
cases.test_reasoning: With three enabled block hooks and restore methods replaced by spies, inherited shutdown on base calls those spies, violating assert_not_called. This is a stable lifecycle boundary test but not GPU-memory or wall-clock evidence.

def _disable(self, *, restore_weights: bool) -> None:
        if not self.enabled and not (
            self._dit_hooks or self._hooked_dit_blocks or self._encoder_modules or self._staged_components
        ):
            return

        steps = []
        if restore_weights:
            steps.extend(("restoring a DiT block", hook.restore_next_block) for hook in self._dit_hooks)
        steps.extend(
            ("removing a DiT block hook", lambda block=block: remove_block_hook(block))
            for block in self._hooked_dit_blocks
        )
        steps.extend(
            (
                "disabling encoder layerwise offload",
                lambda module=module: disable_plan_encoder_layerwise_offload(
                    module,
                    restore_weights=restore_weights,
                ),
            )
            for module in self._encoder_modules
        )
        cleanup_error = run_cleanup_steps(steps)
        if cleanup_error is not None:
            # Keep every host-master reference so a transient teardown error
            # can be retried without losing weights behind placeholders.
            raise RuntimeError("Failed to fully disable layerwise offload") from cleanup_error
        self._blocks.clear()
        self._dit_hooks.clear()
        self._hooked_dit_blocks.clear()
        self._encoder_modules.clear()
        self._staged_components.clear()
        self.enabled = False
        logger.info("Layer-wise offloading disabled")

    def disable(self) -> None:
        self._disable(restore_weights=True)

cases.trigger: Same enabled rank-local offloader shutdown as the historical defect case.
cases.independent_reasoning: The new override dispatches directly to _disable(restore_weights=False). The DiT restoration branch is skipped; the false flag also reaches encoder offload cleanup. Hook removal and ownership clearing remain in the same cleanup routine. The separate disable method still passes true, so normal restoration for re-use remains available.
cases.consequence: The unwanted restore-all-blocks-on-shutdown defect is absent. This is not proof that every cleanup failure, device synchronization, distributed offload path or LTX accuracy test passes.
cases.severity_reason: No severity on a clean case. One specific fixed-path conclusion, not approval or general release readiness.
cases.test_reasoning: The added test checks no restore call and checks enabled/_dit_hooks/_hooked_dit_blocks are cleared. It mocks restore methods and platform streams, making the assertion narrowly appropriate for dispatch and cleanup, while leaving actual device-memory lifetime/timing untested.

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        # Restoring every block copies the whole DiT back onto the device, which
        # only matters for a later ``enable`` and can outlast the executor's
        # shutdown grace period.
